_comment: The `channelConsent` member of PUT /api/v1/contacts/{id} (design D8) and what GET returns. Written 2026-11-05 from Platform main a1fc0481 by reading the code and by one local probe of System.Text.Json with ApiJsonContext's options (camelCase, UseStringEnumConverter, WhenWritingNull); the running host was NOT called (tasks 0.2 measures it). Today UpdateContactRequest (ContactEndpoints.cs:269-279) has no `channelConsent` member, so the member the console sends is dropped and nothing is stored. Contact.ChannelConsent is IReadOnlyDictionary<ChannelType,bool> (Contact.cs:30-31), so GET writes each key as the ChannelType NAME, PascalCase, exactly as `preferredChannel` and `addresses[].channel` are written: `Voice`, `WhatsApp`, `Sms`, `WebChat`, `Email`, `Messenger`, `Instagram`, `Telegram`, `Twitter`, `Video`, `Rcs` (ChannelType.cs). The console's consent page reads and writes lowercase keys (`voice`, `email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `webchat`), so it never finds a recorded consent; the Web child moves it to these names. After this change PUT accepts the member with the SAME names, compared ordinally (case-sensitive); a name that is not a defined ChannelType name (a number such as `0` included) refuses the whole write. Merge semantics: a key present sets that channel; a channel absent from the member keeps its stored value; an absent or null member changes nothing. A value is a JSON boolean. Requires contacts:contact:edit (contact-write-refusals.v1.json). Storage is unchanged: contacts.channel_consent, jsonb keyed by the channel's integer (PostgresContactStore.cs:134-149). Every child change's delta spec must cite these field names and codes VERBATIM.

update.case: the consent page records consent on Voice and Email and refusal on WhatsApp, and sets do-not-contact off

requestFields.channelConsent: object, optional: keys are ChannelType names as GET writes them (case-sensitive), values are booleans. Merged into the stored map
requestFields.doNotContact: boolean, optional: unchanged member; absent or null keeps the stored value

response._note: the Contact read model, unchanged in shape; `channelConsent` now reflects what PUT sent. Members not shown (company, segment, preferredChannel, preferredLanguage, timezone, createdBy, updatedBy, identityLevel) are absent when null, as today

merge.case: a later PUT names only Sms: Voice, Email and WhatsApp keep their values

read._neverRecorded: a contact with no recorded consent answers `channelConsent`: {} (an empty object, never absent: the dictionary is never null). A channel absent from the object has no recorded answer; it is not the same as false

refusals.case: a key that is not a ChannelType name as GET writes it: lowercase, a number, or unknown. Nothing is written, `doNotContact` included
refusals._details: the offending keys, each once, in the order the body names them; the existing ErrorDetailResponse shape (Endpoints/Shared/ErrorResponse.cs), as `reserved-contact-address` uses it
